reflection.text:
Blinded call was Microtubule stabilizers 0.68 vs truth Protein degradation (ALLN) - incorrect. This is phenocopy failure, not absence of phenotype.

What evidence was real:
- There was a strong, dose-related abnormal mitotic/cytokinesis phenotype: nuc_solidity z=-23.7 at 10uM e2 and z=-25.3 at 30uM e9, with dose-response e12 rho=-0.80, plus frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.80 e11, large nuclei nuc_major_axis z=+15.2 / nuc_area z=+9.8 at 3uM e8, and reduced cell counts at high doses 95 cells at 10uM e2 and 103 cells at 30uM e9 vs 186 at 1uM e3 and 303 at 3uM e8. That pattern is consistent with proteasome/calpain inhibition leading to cell-cycle arrest and failed cytokinesis, not only tubulin stabilization. Proteasome inhibitor drugs and the UPS as anticancer target are covered in this run PMID 31479618 PMID 33165832 PMID 39413903, calpain as multi-site regulator of cell cycle PMID 15041468, calpain inhibitor 1 activation of p53-dependent apoptosis PMID 10845425, and protease inhibitor stabilization of p21 and cell-cycle arrest PMID 11807952. Without citation: proteasome block causes accumulation of cyclins, CDK inhibitors and mitotic regulators that secondarily produces multinucleation, low solidity and enlarged nuclei that mimics spindle poisons.
- e3 at 1uM already showed nuc_dna_mean z=-9.5, nuc_solidity z=-5.0, frac_mitotic_like z=-3.8 with lower density, indicating early cytostatic effect, not a clean DMSO-like baseline.

What misled us and why:
- Quantitative tubulin/glcm signal was over-interpreted as on-target. tub_glcm_contrast z=+21.9 at 10uM e2 rising to z=+42.5 at 30uM e9, rho=+0.80 e13, plus act_glcm_contrast z=+14.8 e9 and act_std z=+10.8 e2. I weighted this as direct bundling/polymerization for stabilizers e16/e17. Protein degradation was initially 0.05 e7 and then dropped from the board entirely e16, despite acting via secondary cytoskeletal reorganization after mitotic arrest. I did not consider that texture contrast can rise from cell rounding, compaction and failed division rather than specific microtubule polymer increase.
- Atlas comparison anchored the error. e4 NSC 1/2 Microtubule stabilizers, k-neighbour 6/10 Microtubule stabilizers, 3/10 Protein synthesis, 1/10 Eg5; e10 over 4 wells NSC 2/4 Microtubule stabilizers, k-neighbour 6/10 Microtubule stabilizers, 2/10 Eg5, 2/10 Protein synthesis. Protein degradation never appeared in neighbours. I treated 2/4 NSC and 6/10 kNN as confirmatory and raised stabilizers 0.40->0.68 e7->e16, instead of recognizing atlas has limited proteasome representatives and that Aurora e5, Eg5 and stabilizer classes converge morphologically on multinucleation/solidity.
- Microscopist calls were conflicting and should have lowered confidence: e5 Aurora candidates, e6 unknown, e14 Microtubule stabilizers/unknown, e15 unknown with 9 observations. I resolved conflict by favoring quantitative tubulin, rather than treating "unknown" as support for out-of-atlas mechanism like proteasome.
- Dose-response statistics were non-significant. e11 rho=+0.80 p=0.2, e12 rho=-0.80 p=0.2, e13 rho=+0.80 p=0.2 with n=4 wells. I still used them as key evidence e17. Acquisition choice contributed: list_available_experiments e1 showed 8 doses 0.03-100uM, I sampled only 1, 3, 10, 30uM e2/e3/e8/e9 with no replicates and no low-dose baseline (0.03-0.3uM), so power was inadequate and e8 showing peak cell count 303 broke monotonicity but was listed as contradicting only e16 without follow-up.
- Post-unblinding checks exposed gaps I missed in blinded phase. lookup_compound e18/e19: PubChem CID 6915732, ChEMBL none curated, plus explicit CID mismatch 6915732 vs BBBC021 structure CID 21118339 ((2S)-2-acetamido-4-methyl-N-[(2S)-4-methyl-1-oxo-1-(1-oxohexan-2-ylamino)pentan-2-yl]pentanamide) - I did not pause to verify identity or consider proteasome/calpain inhibitor annotation. search_literature e20/e21 for ALLN and proteasome inhibitor + multinucleation returned 0 hits due to narrow query, while broader queries e22 proteasome inhibitor mechanism 8116 hits/5 returned and e23 calpain inhibitor cell cycle 110 hits/5 returned did return relevant literature PMID 31479618 PMID 33165832 PMID 15041468 etc., but only after submission. I had no proteasome-targeted orthogonal assay in my next-experiment plan - I proposed acetylated/detyrosinated tubulin and polymerization assay, which would have re-confirmed phenocopy rather than testing ubiquitin accumulation or proteasome activity.

Lessons for next run: when extreme solidity loss + tubulin texture + multinucleation proxy co-occur with Eg5/Aurora/stabilizer vote split, retain Protein degradation explicitly; do not discard on atlas absence. Require low-dose and replicate wells to get significant dose-response, and include a proteasome reporter/ubiquitin stain as orthogonal readout before assigning microtubule stabilizer. The review critique in this run was nonsensical (choir IHC, confluence modelling) and should have been ignored.

No clinical interpretation - screening morphology only.
what_was_right: e2/e9 strong dose-dependent loss of nuclear solidity and tubulin texture increase correctly flagged potent mitotic/cytokinesis failure
e8 large nuclei and e11 multinucleate proxy trend flagged polyploidization / failed division seen with proteasome inhibition
e3/e2/e9 reduced nuclei counts flagged antiproliferative effect
what_was_wrong: e13/e12/e11 rho=+/-0.80 p=0.2 treated as confirmatory despite p=0.2 and n=4
e4/e10 NSC 1/2->2/4 and kNN 6/10 stabilizer over-weighted; Protein degradation dropped 0.05->0
tub_glcm_contrast +21.9->+42.5 interpreted as direct stabilization not secondary cytoskeletal compaction
reflection.next_experiment: Test proteasome class directly: repeat dose-response including 0.03-0.3uM DMSO baseline with replicates plus bortezomib/MG132 ALLN reference, measure 20S chymotrypsin-like activity, ubiquitin IHC and p21/p53 accumulation, with same tubulin panel to show secondary vs primary tubulin effect.

## Reflection

Blinded call was Microtubule stabilizers 0.68 vs truth Protein degradation (ALLN) - incorrect. This is phenocopy failure, not absence of phenotype.

What evidence was real:
- There was a strong, dose-related abnormal mitotic/cytokinesis phenotype: nuc_solidity z=-23.7 at 10uM e2 and z=-25.3 at 30uM e9, with dose-response e12 rho=-0.80, plus frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.80 e11, large nuclei nuc_major_axis z=+15.2 / nuc_area z=+9.8 at 3uM e8, and reduced cell counts at high doses 95 cells at 10uM e2 and 103 cells at 30uM e9 vs 186 at 1uM e3 and 303 at 3uM e8. That pattern is consistent with proteasome/calpain inhibition leading to cell-cycle arrest and failed cytokinesis, not only tubulin stabilization. Proteasome inhibitor drugs and the UPS as anticancer target are covered in this run PMID 31479618 PMID 33165832 PMID 39413903, calpain as multi-site regulator of cell cycle PMID 15041468, calpain inhibitor 1 activation of p53-dependent apoptosis PMID 10845425, and protease inhibitor stabilization of p21 and cell-cycle arrest PMID 11807952. Without citation: proteasome block causes accumulation of cyclins, CDK inhibitors and mitotic regulators that secondarily produces multinucleation, low solidity and enlarged nuclei that mimics spindle poisons.
- e3 at 1uM already showed nuc_dna_mean z=-9.5, nuc_solidity z=-5.0, frac_mitotic_like z=-3.8 with lower density, indicating early cytostatic effect, not a clean DMSO-like baseline.

What misled us and why:
- Quantitative tubulin/glcm signal was over-interpreted as on-target. tub_glcm_contrast z=+21.9 at 10uM e2 rising to z=+42.5 at 30uM e9, rho=+0.80 e13, plus act_glcm_contrast z=+14.8 e9 and act_std z=+10.8 e2. I weighted this as direct bundling/polymerization for stabilizers e16/e17. Protein degradation was initially 0.05 e7 and then dropped from the board entirely e16, despite acting via secondary cytoskeletal reorganization after mitotic arrest. I did not consider that texture contrast can rise from cell rounding, compaction and failed division rather than specific microtubule polymer increase.
- Atlas comparison anchored the error. e4 NSC 1/2 Microtubule stabilizers, k-neighbour 6/10 Microtubule stabilizers, 3/10 Protein synthesis, 1/10 Eg5; e10 over 4 wells NSC 2/4 Microtubule stabilizers, k-neighbour 6/10 Microtubule stabilizers, 2/10 Eg5, 2/10 Protein synthesis. Protein degradation never appeared in neighbours. I treated 2/4 NSC and 6/10 kNN as confirmatory and raised stabilizers 0.40->0.68 e7->e16, instead of recognizing atlas has limited proteasome representatives and that Aurora e5, Eg5 and stabilizer classes converge morphologically on multinucleation/solidity.
- Microscopist calls were conflicting and should have lowered confidence: e5 Aurora candidates, e6 unknown, e14 Microtubule stabilizers/unknown, e15 unknown with 9 observations. I resolved conflict by favoring quantitative tubulin, rather than treating "unknown" as support for out-of-atlas mechanism like proteasome.
- Dose-response statistics were non-significant. e11 rho=+0.80 p=0.2, e12 rho=-0.80 p=0.2, e13 rho=+0.80 p=0.2 with n=4 wells. I still used them as key evidence e17. Acquisition choice contributed: list_available_experiments e1 showed 8 doses 0.03-100uM, I sampled only 1, 3, 10, 30uM e2/e3/e8/e9 with no replicates and no low-dose baseline (0.03-0.3uM), so power was inadequate and e8 showing peak cell count 303 broke monotonicity but was listed as contradicting only e16 without follow-up.
- Post-unblinding checks exposed gaps I missed in blinded phase. lookup_compound e18/e19: PubChem CID 6915732, ChEMBL none curated, plus explicit CID mismatch 6915732 vs BBBC021 structure CID 21118339 ((2S)-2-acetamido-4-methyl-N-[(2S)-4-methyl-1-oxo-1-(1-oxohexan-2-ylamino)pentan-2-yl]pentanamide) - I did not pause to verify identity or consider proteasome/calpain inhibitor annotation. search_literature e20/e21 for ALLN and proteasome inhibitor + multinucleation returned 0 hits due to narrow query, while broader queries e22 proteasome inhibitor mechanism 8116 hits/5 returned and e23 calpain inhibitor cell cycle 110 hits/5 returned did return relevant literature PMID 31479618 PMID 33165832 PMID 15041468 etc., but only after submission. I had no proteasome-targeted orthogonal assay in my next-experiment plan - I proposed acetylated/detyrosinated tubulin and polymerization assay, which would have re-confirmed phenocopy rather than testing ubiquitin accumulation or proteasome activity.

Lessons for next run: when extreme solidity loss + tubulin texture + multinucleation proxy co-occur with Eg5/Aurora/stabilizer vote split, retain Protein degradation explicitly; do not discard on atlas absence. Require low-dose and replicate wells to get significant dose-response, and include a proteasome reporter/ubiquitin stain as orthogonal readout before assigning microtubule stabilizer. The review critique in this run was nonsensical (choir IHC, confluence modelling) and should have been ignored.

No clinical interpretation - screening morphology only.

What was right:
- e2/e9 strong dose-dependent loss of nuclear solidity and tubulin texture increase correctly flagged potent mitotic/cytokinesis failure
- e8 large nuclei and e11 multinucleate proxy trend flagged polyploidization / failed division seen with proteasome inhibition
- e3/e2/e9 reduced nuclei counts flagged antiproliferative effect

What was wrong or missed:
- e13/e12/e11 rho=+/-0.80 p=0.2 treated as confirmatory despite p=0.2 and n=4
- e4/e10 NSC 1/2->2/4 and kNN 6/10 stabilizer over-weighted; Protein degradation dropped 0.05->0
- tub_glcm_contrast +21.9->+42.5 interpreted as direct stabilization not secondary cytoskeletal compaction

Proposed next experiment: Test proteasome class directly: repeat dose-response including 0.03-0.3uM DMSO baseline with replicates plus bortezomib/MG132 ALLN reference, measure 20S chymotrypsin-like activity, ubiquitin IHC and p21/p53 accumulation, with same tubulin panel to show secondary vs primary tubulin effect.
